what_changed: From the 2017-18 collection, all degree-granting institutions report full-year entering cohorts (before, schools on standard terms reported fall cohorts), and each of the four cohorts is split into Pell and non-Pell recipients. Cohort codes changed from 1-4 to 10-52.
note_shown: Outcome Measures cohorts changed in 2017-18: every school now reports students who entered over a full year, split by Pell status. Earlier figures used fall entering cohorts at many schools.
source: NCES, IPEDS overview (Handbook of Survey Methods, 2019), pages 4 and 8; OMCHRT codes in the 2015-16 to 2017-18 codebooks

what_changed: A new hire is someone hired between November 1 and October 31; before, the window was July 1 to October 31.
note_shown: IPEDS changed the hiring window for new hires; its documentation gives different first years, from 2016-17 to 2020-21.
source: 2016-17 codebook, table S2016_NH. Later codebooks disagree on the first year (S2017_NH says before fall 2017, S2020_NH says before fall 2020, S2021_NH says before fall 2016): to confirm

applies_to: Faculty not on the tenure track
what_changed: Faculty not on the tenure track are split by contract length (multi-year, indefinite, annual, less than annual); multi-year and indefinite contracts are new for 2016.
note_shown: From 2016-17, faculty not on the tenure track are split by length of contract; earlier years group them differently.
source: 2016-17 codebook, tables EAP2016 and S2017_NH; faculty-status codes 44 and 45 absent from 2015-16 (code_changes.csv)

what_changed: Certificates of less than one year are divided into certificates of less than 12 weeks and certificates of at least 12 weeks but less than one year (awards of 2019-20, reported in the 2020-21 release).
note_shown: From the 2020-21 release, certificates of less than one year are split into those under 12 weeks and those of 12 weeks to under a year.
source: 2020-21 codebook, tables C2020_A, C2020_C and C2020DEP

what_changed: Programs are classified by the 2020 Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP 2020), replacing CIP 2010, which was used for completions collected from 2009-10 to 2018-19. No crosswalk is applied (owner decision 4b).
note_shown: Field-of-study codes changed to the 2020 classification (CIP 2020) from the 2020-21 release. The changes were mostly at the detailed six-digit level; the broad two-digit fields used in the field-of-study breakdown changed much less.
source: 2020-21 codebook, table C2020_A. Whether fall enrollment by major (EFCP) changed at the same time is to confirm

what_changed: Undergraduate headcounts are reported by attendance status and degree-seeking status, in a new level column (EFFYALEV). Before, only all students, undergraduates and graduate students (EFFYLEV).
note_shown: From the 2020-21 release, 12-month enrollment is reported in more detail by student level; earlier years have only all students, undergraduates and graduate students.

what_changed: From fiscal year 2020, scholarships and fellowships data contain the amount of discounts and allowances attributed to each source.
note_shown: From fiscal year 2020, scholarships and fellowships by source include the discounts and allowances attributed to each source.
source: 2020-21 codebook, tables F1920_F1A, F1920_F2 and F1920_F3 (the same sentence in each)

what_changed: Students who do not fit the IPEDS binary gender (another gender) are reported for undergraduate and graduate totals from fall 2022; from 2023-24, values of 1 to 4 are not reported.
note_shown: From fall 2022, IPEDS also counts students who do not fit the men and women categories, so men plus women can be less than the total.
source: 2022-23 codebook, table EF2022A; 2023-24 codebook, tables EF2023A and ADM2023

applies_to: Any figure whose period overlaps March 2020 to June 2022
what_changed: The pandemic period. Not a definition change. Attached by the period a figure covers: fall 2020 and fall 2021; academic and fiscal years 2019-20, 2020-21 and 2021-22.
note_shown: Figures covering 2020 to 2022 reflect the COVID-19 pandemic period.
source: Owner decisions 5b and of the Part 5b report (2026-11-22)

what_changed: Undergraduates are reported separately as degree/certificate-seeking and non-degree-seeking: grant aid and the Pell and loan percents from the 2022-23 release (aid year 2021-22); Pell and loan counts and amounts from the 2023-24 release (aid year 2022-23). The all-undergraduate totals did not change definition: the parts add to the totals and the national totals move smoothly (docs/reports/stage5b/aid_split_*.csv).
note_shown: IPEDS began reporting degree-seeking and non-degree-seeking undergraduates separately in the 2022-23 release for grant aid and the Pell and loan percents, and in the 2023-24 release for Pell and loan counts and amounts. The all-undergraduate totals are unchanged.
source: 2022-23 codebook, table SFA2122_P1; 2023-24 codebook, table SFA2223_P1; scripts/aid_split_check.py

what_changed: National grant recipients rose 4.8% in aid year 2021-22 and fell 9.6% in 2022-23, at 3,331 schools down and 1,934 up. The codebook gives no reason.
note_shown: The number of students receiving grant aid rose in 2021-22 and fell in 2022-23 at many schools; IPEDS does not give a reason.

what_changed: Cost of attendance counts food and housing in place of room and board, adds a food and housing charge for students living off campus with family, and the cost and aid tables are reorganised (mapped in measure_history.csv).
note_shown: From 2024-25, cost of attendance counts food and housing in place of room and board, and adds a charge for students living off campus with family.
source: 2024-25 codebook, table COST1_2024 and the list of new variables

applies_to: Salaries as a percent of expenses (finance)
what_changed: The derived percentages of expenses spent on salaries, wages and benefits, by function, are replaced by salaries and wages only: from fiscal year 2016, IPEDS no longer collects benefits by function. The 24 successor pairs are approved.
note_shown: From fiscal year 2016, IPEDS reports the share of expenses spent on salaries and wages, without benefits; earlier years include benefits.

what_changed: F1C195 (total expenses, all other) continues as F1C19OT (other natural expenses). From fiscal year 2016 IPEDS stopped collecting several natural classifications by function, which may have shifted what is counted as other expenses.
note_shown: The 2016-17 finance changes may have shifted what is counted as other expenses.
source: 2016-17 codebook, table F1516_F1A; owner decision on the successor list (2026-11-22)
